name: Slow-flow malformation, lymphatic type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and radiological criteria for lymphatic slow-flow malformations

criteria.description: Presence of soft, compressible, non-pulsatile masses consistent with lymphatic malformations
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating characteristic cystic, septated lesions with slow-flow lymphatic channels
Histological confirmation showing dilated lymphatic vessels lined by endothelial cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical presentation plus characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not mandatory if clinical and imaging criteria are met.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically present at or shortly after birth

common.notes: Often involving extremities or head and neck

common.symptomName: Pain or discomfort due to mass effect
Recurrent episodes of inflammation or infection (lymphangitis)
Functional impairment related to lesion size and location
searchTerms: loss of function from lesion size
movement problems due to lesion location

occasional.notes: Lymphatic system involvement implied under immunological
searchTerms: fluid buildup in limb from lymph blockage

rare.symptomName: Airway obstruction due to cervical lymphatic malformation
searchTerms: airway narrowing due to neck swelling

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to mass effect
searchTerms: nerve symptoms due to lesion pressure
brain or nerve issues from tumor

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary infection or bleeding
Possible elevated inflammatory markers during infection
imaging: MRI showing multiloculated cystic lesions with fluid-fluid levels
Ultrasound demonstrating anechoic or hypoechoic cystic spaces with septations
Lymphoscintigraphy may show impaired lymphatic drainage
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Histopathology reveals dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells
Fluid aspirate typically clear or straw-colored lymphatic fluid

distinguishingFeatures: Slower flow venous channels rather than lymphatic
More complex clinical and imaging features

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of lesion suggesting hemorrhage or infection
Airway compromise in cervical or facial lesions
references: Orphanet: Slow-flow malformation, lymphatic type - ORPHA:211255
Wassef M, Blei F, Adams DM, et al. Vascular Anomalies Classification: Recommendations From the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015
